critique:
field remaining_targets, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  When the goal requested the red-covering container, two containers moved around one another and finished at the same unordered pair of occupied positions. The policy selected the red container's original position, [111, 111], and wrote [[111, 111]], whereas the demonstration identity assignment requires [[99, 155]]. This exposes a PREDICTABILITY failure in interpreting exchanges, leading to the wrong target. Clarify that returning to the same set of occupied positions does not mean identities have returned: count exchanges by the paths of the individual containers, not by recurrence of the unordered position set. Across each movement interval, follow the full directed paths through intermediate frames to the settled endpoints. In the relevant pattern, the red identity follows [111, 111], [99, 117], [91, 137], then the endpoint near [99, 155]; this is one exchange, not two. Keep remaining_targets as the ordered list of final container locations for requested pickups not yet completed. Initialize it after tracking the entire demonstration, for example [[99, 155]], and remove its first entry only at the decision showing the completed requested pickup. Release leaves it unchanged. No additional memory field is needed.

field remaining_targets, POLICY PROMPT
  When asked to pick up the red-covering container after a demonstration in which a moving pair ended at the same unordered positions it initially occupied, the policy chose the original red position and wrote [[111, 111]] instead of the required [[99, 155]]. The generic continuity and exchange instructions left the sparse-frame identity association unresolved, breaking PREDICTABILITY and consequently target selection. Clarify initialization using the demonstration visible at the first decision: associate cubes with their covers, then track each moving pair over the entire interval from departure to settling. Use the direction of travel across intermediate frames to resolve the endpoint assignment; do not reset identity to the nearest original position, or count a return of the unordered position set as a second exchange. For example, a cover starting at [111, 111] and moving through [99, 117] and [91, 137] continues toward the endpoint near [99, 155], while the other cover takes the complementary path. Only a further observed exchange of those tracked identities restores their original assignment. Write the resulting ordered list of requested final locations, such as [[99, 155]], including the pickup selected now. Retain the existing observable update rule: remove the head when the current execution frames show the successful descent, closure around the target, and lift; do not remove it when merely selecting a pickup, and preserve the list through release. The list remains the only persistent field; intermediate tracks are computed from the currently shown demonstration.
